title: How the Water Cycle Moves Water Around Earth

Sources: United States Geological Survey https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/water-cycle and National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/the-water-cycle/ #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Where does the rain that falls today go next? The water cycle is the story of where Earth's water is stored and how it moves between those places. Sunlight and gravity keep that water moving all the time. Evaporation from oceans, seas, lakes and rivers supplies most of the moisture in the air. Plants release most of the rest through tiny pores in their leaves, a process called transpiration. Rising air currents carry water vapor high into the atmosphere, where cool air makes condensation into cloud droplets more likely, and precipitation carries the water back to the surface. Over land, precipitation can evaporate back to the atmosphere, seep into the ground, or run off into rivers and streams, and almost all of the water eventually reaches the oceans. Oceans hold almost all of Earth's water. At any moment the air holds only a minute fraction of Earth's water, yet far more water cycles through it every year.
